blocks.h2: Filtration Options for Lincoln Park Homes

tiles.body: Very clean water from a dedicated faucet.
For single-family homes and whole buildings.

bodies: We test what affects your plumbing and your taste, like hardness, chlorine and sediment, and explain the results plainly.

Chicago's water comes from Lake Michigan and is treated and tested by the city. The pipes inside an older building are a separate question. For health-related testing, a state-certified lab can run a full panel, and we'll point you to one.

blocks.intro: The city treats the water. What happens inside your building depends on its pipes.

items.body: Galvanized and other older piping can affect taste and pressure.
An under-sink filter is easy to add in a unit.
Filters and softeners reduce scale in heaters and dishwashers.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.body: In a condo, a whole-house filter may not be practical if the main shutoff for your unit is hard to reach. Point-of-use filters work well instead. An under-sink filter or reverse osmosis system at the kitchen sink covers drinking and cooking water, and a filtered showerhead can reduce chlorine in the bath. We'll match the system to your unit and your building's rules.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Filtration
blocks.body: Under-sink and reverse osmosis systems are the most common in condos. Whole-house systems depend on access to the main line. We check your space and quote a flat price.

blocks.h2: Water Filtration Questions From Lincoln Park Homeowners

items.q: Do I need a filter for Chicago water?
items.preview: It's treated. Filters are for taste and extra peace of mind.
items.answer: Chicago's water is treated and tested. Most people who filter do it for taste or peace of mind, especially in older buildings.

items.q: Can I install a filter in my condo?
items.answer: Yes. Under-sink and reverse osmosis filters are easy to add inside a unit.

items.preview: A multi-stage filter for drinking water.
items.answer: A system that pushes water through very fine filters and stores it for a dedicated faucet. It's for drinking and cooking water.

items.q: How often do filters need changing?
items.answer: Under-sink cartridges usually every several months.

items.q: Will a reverse osmosis system fit under my sink?
items.answer: Usually, with a compact tank. We'll check the space first.

items.q: How much does water filtration cost in Lincoln Park?
items.preview: It depends on the system. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the system and installation. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we install.
